headline: Ratchet & Clank's native PAL port gains walking, jumping and checkpoint respawning
summary: The native-port scaffolding lands in #3, removing the earlier emulator experiment and setting up games from the player's disc. Ratchet & Clank PAL then gains enough movement and checkpoint code to complete a Veldin fall-and-respawn check and walk, jump and land afterwards (#5). Windows build fixes and New Game initialisation also land (#4). This is direct development on master rather than its usual release-pull-request activity.
highlights: The launcher offers Build the game and Rebuild. Its Windows Play action is still marked unverified and needs extracted data and level exports.
The renderer gains movies, live character animation, original lighting and fog, effects, particles and the flight world's sky.
A debug level selector and a developer Planets menu can start levels directly. Missing C routines are logged and skipped by default, so reaching a level does not establish complete gameplay.
The native port is still silent at this stage: stream stand-ins satisfy loading logic while the sound engine remains unfinished.
#4 reports a passing Windows release build and test suite, while #5 describes validation from a clean checkout using the bundled PAL sources.
